title: The Gucci Ring Across the Table
lessons: A coworker angles their hand across the conference table to show off an 18-karat gold-trimmed Oura ring from the Gucci collaboration.
The player checks Oura during a demanding workday and opens the Stress Management hub.

text: A coworker angles their hand across the conference table so the gold catches the light, and asks if you've seen the Gucci ones.

entry-first-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Someone in my meeting just did a wedding-ring reveal with a fitness tracker.

entry-first-2.speaker: OURA
text: That would be the Gucci edition. Eighteen-karat gold trim, limited run. I didn't expect it to be shown off in a meeting. I'm not unhappy about it.

entry-first-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: It sold out that fast?

entry-first-4.speaker: OURA
text: Within days. It comes back as a holiday drop because it keeps selling out. People wait for the gold one while the plain one sits in stock.

choice-first.speaker: OURA
text: They're still holding their hand out. Say something before it gets awkward.

choices.text: A ring people fight over is still a ring people trust.
That's jewelry hype. It doesn't tell me anything about the ring itself.
I don't want a waitlist standing between me and my own sleep data.

first-1.speaker: OURA
text: Then wanting it and using it can live on the same hand. Most of my rings start with the first one.

first-2.speaker: OURA
text: Fair. The scarcity is doing marketing, not measuring.

first-2-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: So the gold trim and the sleep score are two different pitches.

first-2-2.speaker: OURA
text: Guilty. Scarcity sells before sleep ever gets involved.

first-3.speaker: OURA
text: Then buy me when the gold wears off, not before. The plain one reads your finger exactly the same.
Bad workday. You open the app under the desk and find the Stress Management hub.

entry-return-1.speaker: OURA
text: This is physiological stress, not me reading your inbox.

entry-return-2.speaker: PLAYER
text: Important distinction. My inbox is doing enough.

entry-return-3.speaker: OURA
text: It shows today next to the last few weeks, so you can see whether this is one bad afternoon or the shape of the month.

entry-return-4.speaker: PLAYER
text: And you still don't know what caused it.

entry-return-5.speaker: OURA
text: Correct. I know signals. I do not know your boss.

choice-return.speaker: OURA
text: You've looked at it three times in ten minutes.

choices.text: I like seeing whether this week is actually wearing me down.
Looking at a stress chart is stressing me out more.
I don't want my workday turned into another health dashboard.

return-1.speaker: OURA
text: Then it's putting a shape on something you already felt in your shoulders. I can't fix the week. I can show you it's a week.

return-2.speaker: OURA
text: Yes. Checking me can become its own stressor. I've watched it happen and I couldn't do anything about it.

return-3.speaker: OURA
text: Then close the hub. Not every feeling needs a graph.
